about: Which library constraints a Learning Goal may select, by owner ruling, with the manipulations its context names evaluated against the knowledge that exists. Ids, citations, statuses and his words only: nothing here is a value, a mapping to an Environmental Manipulation or Affordance Target id, or a candidate pool. Where a goal has an entry, selection draws its constraints from authorizedConstraints and from nothing else (not the wording pool, not the Game Problem's Coverage row), in both pathways. authorizedConstraints null means the record has not yet evaluated which constraints the knowledge justifies: a knowledge gap (NO_AUTHORIZED_CONSTRAINTS), never a fallback. A list (with its finding) is the evaluation; an EMPTY list means none is justified, and under the general principle below the goal is selected with no library constraint. The principle is recorded once, here, and applies to every record alike: no goal is special-cased. ADDED 15 October 2026 (stage H3, his 16 October reply, item 10: 'The decisions above should be interpreted as either: General learning-design principles. Provisional realization choices for the first activity. Existing knowledge relationships that require verification. Genuine implementation or knowledge gaps. Please keep those categories distinct.'): every manipulation and provisional choice names its CATEGORY (what its authority is: PROVISIONAL_REALIZATION_CHOICE, his choice for this activity; EXISTING_KNOWLEDGE_TO_VERIFY, the game form, the context or the session, offered for his verification; GENUINE_GAP, nothing settles it; a GENERAL_PRINCIPLE is recorded once, at the top) beside its STATUS (whether the activity can carry it now). A status of MISSING_KNOWLEDGE or MISSING_CAPABILITY means the activity his rulings ask for needs it and it is not in place; it names the decisions and capabilities (gaps, defined in the record) that would supply it, and the build refuses the goal naming each one rather than build an activity that solves a different problem. existingKnowledge lists what existing knowledge already authorizes for the activity, with its sources. The decision and capability ids (D1-D7, M1-M8) and their one-line descriptions are OUR wording, as put to him; none is his. AMENDED 15 October 2026 (stage K2), narrowly, for his reply filed 17 October 2026: 'The priority remains producing one complete, representative Play Out from the Back activity through the normal generation pathway, without introducing unnecessary architecture or treating this first realization as the canonical version of the Learning Goal.' A record may name ONE provisional realization (provisionalRealization: an id in docs/audits/conformance/stage-b/provisional-realizations.json). That file, not this one, holds his provisional realization choices as contract items in his words; derivation adds them only for the goal whose record names the realization, every one carries the category PROVISIONAL_REALIZATION_CHOICE into the game, and none is canonical knowledge of the context. This record still holds no value: it names the realization, as it names a constraint. AMENDED 15 October 2026 (stage K4), narrowly, for his replies filed 17 and 18 October 2026: the file now records ONE mapping to an Environmental Manipulation, the context-manipulation relationship he asked for and then confirmed (contextManipulationRelationships; 17 October, D6: 'Please authorize this initial numerical asymmetry through the appropriate existing knowledge relationship, rather than hardcoding it to Play Out from the Back.'; 18 October, item 5: 'Goalkeeper Build-Out with Participant Composition.'), his allocation principle once (allocationPrinciple), and, in a record, the adjustments he authorized for that goal's activity, in his words (authorizedAdjustments). An adjustment names a count only where his words do. The starting counts themselves stay in the provisional realization, never here. AMENDED 21 October 2026 (stage 2G of the communication work), narrowly, for his reply filed 23 October 2026, item 2: 'Please authorize marking once whenever the system can establish that the physical markings occupy the same locations across all blocks. This should be a general presentation rule, not something requiring my approval for each configuration.' The provisional choice added to A01's record on 21 October 2026 (stage 2D, for his reply filed 22 October 2026, item 7: the code MARK_UNION_ONCE with the 40 × 30 m area it applied to) is removed, with the value and appliesTo fields the loader admitted only for it; the loader now refuses either field on any provisional choice. Marking once is a general presentation rule (back/src/system/rendering/physical-layout.ts), recorded per configuration nowhere, so no value of that kind is held here. The knowledge is unchanged: each block keeps its own targets and relationships (his item 2: 'The distinction between physical markings and role-specific scoring relationships must remain intact in the underlying knowledge.'). AMENDED 26 October 2026 (Stage F), narrowly, for his replies filed 25 and 26 October 2026: the file records ONE context SCORING relationship (contextScoringRelationships; his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 1: 'The opposing team may have a different primary scoring event where authorized by the selected context.'), and A01's record names its realizations as an ordered list (realizations) instead of one (his reply filed 25 October 2026, item 4: 'I approve retaining both alternatives.'): the goal version first, waiting on two decisions of his (D-GOAL-SUITABILITY, D-PENALTY-AREA) and so listed and never tried, then the zone version. The record still holds no value.

libraryConstraintPrinciple.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (called his 16 October reply, to keep it apart from his first 15 October reply), item 1
libraryConstraintPrinciple.principle: A library constraint is not mandatory unless its inclusion is justified by the approved knowledge and intended learning environment.
words: I agree that an activity should not require two to four library constraints simply to satisfy an engine quota.

The game form and its inherent conditions may already create the affordances needed for the Learning Goal. Additional constraints should be selected because they serve a documented learning-design purpose, not because the engine requires a particular number.
However, I want the underlying principle to apply generally:
A library constraint is not mandatory unless its inclusion is justified by the approved knowledge and intended learning environment.

I understand that applying this immediately to every Learning Goal could interrupt existing functionality. We can implement the correction incrementally, but please don't establish Play Out from the Back as a permanent special-case exception.
The engine should continue enforcing structural validity and any genuinely required conditions.
libraryConstraintPrinciple.appliedAs: Every Learning Goal whose authorization record has evaluated its authorized constraints and found none justified (an empty list) is selected with its game form and lenses and no library constraint; derivation, realization and every gate still run on it. Applied incrementally, as his words allow: a goal reaches it only once it has a record, and goals without one keep the vocabulary pool and the two-to-four rule. The lens rule (two or three) is unchanged: his item 1 speaks of library constraints, not lenses.

allocationPrinciple.principle: The important principle is that player allocation should reflect representative numerical relationships, not default to equal outfield numbers regardless of the Learning Goal.
words: In match play, teams building from the back commonly have more players available in their defensive third than the opposition initially commits to pressing.
A building-team numerical advantage is therefore not necessarily an artificial simplification. It can be representative of the actual performance environment.
The important principle is that player allocation should reflect representative numerical relationships, not default to equal outfield numbers regardless of the Learning Goal.
Please authorize this initial numerical asymmetry through the appropriate existing knowledge relationship, rather than hardcoding it to Play Out from the Back.
Please do not assign a goalkeeper an inactive role solely to preserve a symmetrical team structure.
allocationPrinciple.appliedAs: Recorded once, with no goal id, and applied without one. Equal outfield numbers stay the possession game's own knowledge (GF2-14.b): ruling C56 lets that item defer only in a composition where another selected contribution authors the outfield count per team and cites a CONFIRMED relationship below that authorizes the row (back/src/system/derivation/realization-deferral.ts); it is then listed as the alternative. The roster reads per-team counts from such items alone and refuses rather than choose: an allocation that fits no authored count is refused for that session (CONFIGURATION_DOES_NOT_FIT), and authored per-team counts with the equal-numbers requirement still in force are refused (NO_AUTHORIZED_ASYMMETRY). A goalkeeper available and not involved is counted among the outfield players by the roster's availability-is-not-involvement rule (his ruling of 30 September), so no goalkeeper is idled to make the teams symmetric; that is the only reading given to his last sentence, kept to what he said.

ruling: I approve Gain Access as the primary Game Problem for Play Out from the Back, based on the approved Goalkeeper Build-Out context and its scoring condition.

Create Space remains relevant as a potential means of solving the problem, but I agree that we should not assign it as a secondary Game Problem at this stage. Let's retain our existing decision to defer secondary Game Problems.
This resolves the Cycle 8 translation gap for this Learning Goal through the approved context rather than inference from the goal's wording.
One important distinction: approving Gain Access does not automatically authorize the candidate constraints currently derived from vocabulary coverage.
I would prefer that the activity's constraints be selected based on their documented relationship to the approved context, Game Problem, and target affordances.

The context's existing manipulations—starting positions, field dimensions, progression references, defensive numbers, goalkeeper positioning, overloads, and support spacing—are appropriate candidates for evaluation. However, they should not automatically become selected constraints simply because they appear in that list.
Please identify the smallest set of authorized manipulations needed to create a representative build-out problem, and flag any missing knowledge rather than filling gaps through inference.

provisionalChoices.choice: An asymmetrical build-out-versus-press structure: one team builds out, the other presses to prevent progression, regain possession and exploit the regain, and the teams exchange roles over successive episodes or blocks.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 2
provisionalChoices.words: For the first demonstration, I favor an asymmetrical game structure. One team begins by building out from its goalkeeper or a controlled defensive restart. The opposing team attempts to prevent progression, regain possession, and exploit the regain. The teams exchange roles over successive episodes or blocks so both experience the Learning Goal. This is a provisional realization choice, not a universal requirement for Play Out from the Back.
provisionalChoices.note: Carried since 15 October 2026 by the provisional realization A01-R1: the two roles and the coach-called exchange (A01-R1-B1-1, A01-R1-B1-2, A01-R1-B3-1; his D2(a), reply filed 17 October 2026, 'Approve D2(a): Coach-controlled blocks. One team builds out while the other presses. The coach determines when the teams exchange roles.') on capability M1 (role blocks, register version 10, stage K3) and M2 (team designations, register version 9, stage K2), and the role-specific objectives (his D7, 'I approve your proposed role-specific wording, with the adjustments established above.') through the targets keyed by role. Moved at stage K6, 15 October 2026: it should have moved at stage K3, and the K4 and K5 reviews flagged it as stale. Until then: Nothing in the knowledge attaches a fact to one team by its role for a block, and nothing represents blocks or exchanging roles (measured 15 October 2026: the roster gives every team one equal count, and a team-specific selector is refused as not settled). Whether roles swap by block or by episode is decision D2; the pressing team's objective and how it is named (his 9.6, revised by us) wait on his acknowledgement, D7. His item 2 also: 'Symmetrical, continuous games should remain legitimate alternatives when they create the appropriate learning environment.'

provisionalChoices.choice: An intermediate progression reference or target for the build-out, not a distant terminal end zone; no mandated midfield and no universal depth.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 4
provisionalChoices.words: I therefore favor an intermediate progression reference or target over a distant terminal end zone for this first activity.
provisionalChoices.note: The choice stands; WHERE the target sits is the gap recorded on 'progression references' below (D3). It supersedes the far-end 5 m prototype of his 15 October item 2. Amended 17 October 2026 (stage M4): D3 is settled - his reply filed 17 October 2026, D3, and his reply filed 18 October 2026, item 3 ('Building team's progression target: begins at the pressure reference.') - and carried by A01-R1-S5-2; the gaps list shows D3 as settled, with his words.

provisionalChoices.choice: After a defensive regain, the pressing team plays for a target area toward a higher attacking player or attacking space, reached by controlled entry; not, for now, a goalkeeper-defended goal.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 5
provisionalChoices.words: After considering the available targets, I favor a target area representing successful progression toward a higher attacking player or attacking space for the first demonstration. This target would be available following a defensive regain. Success should be possible through controlled entry, either by carrying the ball or by passing to a teammate who receives under control.
provisionalChoices.note: Each team already has its own target in a different place (ruling C42), so the area itself is representable; its depth is the gap on 'progression references' below (D3), and whether it is live throughout the pressing team's block is part of D7 (amended 17 October 2026, stage M4: both settled - the depth by his reply filed 18 October 2026, item 3, 'Pressing team's post-regain target area: 5 m deep at the building team's end.', carried by A01-R1-S5-3; the objective by his D7 and his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2, 'The pressing team retains its separate objective of regaining possession and attacking the 5 m target area.'). Item 5 also refuses a rule requiring a teammate to receive inside the target after a regain there, and asks for no transition window, pass sequence, timing condition or automatic high-regain bonus; none is recorded. Amended 17 October 2026 (stage M2): his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2, now counts a controlled regain inside this area as a score for the pressing team ("For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession."), carried by A01-R1-V27-1 with V29-1, V30-1 and V31-1; it earns the ordinary value of a score, so still no bonus is recorded, and no teammate is required to receive after it ("without requiring an arbitrary additional pass or dribble"). A target player, small goal or goalkeeper-defended goal stays an alternative, not excluded: alongside a zone for the other team it would need a scoring event kind per team, which one primary scoring event per game (SD-06) does not allow today. SUPERSEDED FOR THE GOAL VERSION, 26 October 2026 (Stage F): his reply filed 25 October 2026, item 3, "I approve a goalkeeper-protected physical goal as an authorized alternative to the pressing team's 5 m target zone within the Goalkeeper Build-Out context.", and item 4, "I approve retaining both alternatives."; one primary scoring event per role is approved (his reply filed 25 October 2026, item 2; his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 1). The record lists the goal version (A01-R2) first and this zone version (A01-R1) second (realizations); this choice is A01-R1's, and A01-R2 withdraws the area and its scoring items.

provisionalChoices.choice: A new build-out episode begins with a goalkeeper or controlled defensive restart once the previous episode has meaningfully concluded, without interrupting a promising attack; after a score play stops and restarts, at a location the coach selects.
provisionalChoices.citedAs: his reply received 15 October 2026 (16 October reply), item 6 and 6.ii
provisionalChoices.words: For this first activity, I favor returning to a goalkeeper or controlled defensive restart when an episode has meaningfully concluded. However, the activity should not interrupt a promising attacking or counterattacking opportunity simply because the initial build-out objective has been achieved. … After a score: Yes, play stops and restarts. The coach can select an appropriate authorized restart location, consistent with the intended build-out situation.
provisionalChoices.note: Nothing in the knowledge means 'the episode has concluded' (the trigger list is closed: a score, the ball going out, a change of possession, a completed pass and the like), and the game holds no start or score transition element, so no build-out episode can begin (measured 15 October 2026: GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE). The restart location as the coach's choice extends what a coach decides and needs his ruling (D5, M3). Whether reaching the progression target is a score that stops play is D1: his 6.ii answered a question we had framed around the far-end zone. The possession game's ordinary out-of-play rule is not the preferred restart here (6.iii). Carried since 15 October 2026 (stage K5), on his 17 October D1, D5, M3 and M4 and his 18 October items 2 and 4: A01-R1's start, after-score and coach-judged conclusion transitions stop and restart play, are awarded to the team holding the building role and taken by its goalkeeper from the feet at a location the coach chooses (A01-R1-T1-1..3, T6-1, T7-1, T2-1, T3-1, T4-1, T5-1); the coach-judged conclusion is the trigger registered for his M4 (register version 12); ball out is an ordinary restart partitioned by who touched it last - a throw-in on the touchline, the coach's method on the end line - that continues the episode off the pressing team and ends the build-out off the building team (A01-R1-T1-4..7 and their items); and the build-out begin condition is typed in his acknowledged wording (ruling C58), so GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE passes in both blocks with one awardee. That the end-line location is the coach's too, and who takes an end-line restart, were our readings put to him for a one-line confirmation; CONFIRMED in his reply filed 19 October 2026, items 3 A and 3 B (recorded 17 October 2026, stage M4, on A01-R1-T4-3, A01-R1-T5-3 and A01-R1-T3-3). Until stage K5 this was MISSING_CAPABILITY, waiting on D1, D5, M3 and M4.

provisionalChoices.choice: A controlled regain inside the pressing team's own target area counts as a score for the pressing team, of ordinary value, when it genuinely establishes possession; a contested touch, deflection or loose ball does not.
provisionalChoices.words: For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession. A contested touch, deflection, or loose ball should not qualify. This gives the pressing team a meaningful incentive to recognize and exploit high-regain opportunities without requiring an arbitrary additional pass or dribble. This is a provisional scoring choice for the current realization, not a universal rule equating every regain with successful progression.
provisionalChoices.note: Added 17 October 2026 (stage M2). Carried by A01-R1-V27-1 with V29-1, V30-1 and V31-1 (register row V27: an occurrence that also counts as the one primary event and earns its value; the name and that reading are ours, SD-113), for the pressing role only, and checked by GA-ONE-PRIMARY-EVENT in both blocks. The zone entry keeps its meaning, so his 17 October D7 on entry stands. Said to the coach only in approved words: until he approves a sentence, the activity is refused at communication naming the element's four fields. Amended 18 October 2026 (design step L14): he approved the sentence, his reply filed 20 October 2026, item 1 ("Pressing team's regain score — Approved as written."), now entry A01-W2 in approved-coach-wording.json, so the four fields are said and the activity is served; the same reply, item 2, gave in his own wording the sentence that a regain does not restore the building team's opportunity (entry A01-W3). His approval covers those sentences only: "I understand that the remaining coach-facing sentences are still drafts, so this approval applies specifically to the two scoring statements, not yet to the entire activity." SCOPED TO THE ZONE VERSION, 26 October 2026 (Stage F): his reply filed 25 October 2026, item 3, "The existing automatic controlled-regain score inside the 5 m zone does not carry into this version.", and his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 12, "The former 5 m target-zone scoring lines should not carry into it." existingKnowledge.what: Two opposed teams, the opposition live and able to deny, redirect or reverse progression.
Each team attacks its own target, the two targets in different places.
One scoring event kind serves both targets, and the context approves a zone entered or a line crossed.

existingKnowledge.what: The build-out scoring condition (controlled arrival beyond the initial pressure or progression line; a long clearance does not count) applies only to build-out episodes.
existingKnowledge.note: Carried by the engine since 15 October 2026; with no transition that can begin a build-out episode the build refused at structure (GA-EPISODE-REACHABLE) until stage K5 (15 October 2026): the provisional realization's start, after-score and coach-judged restarts now begin the build-out episode, and the begin condition is typed (ruling C58).

existingKnowledge.what: Play continues after a change of possession, and a regain begins a new episode.

Pressure is bounded on both sides: the building team has stability enough to organize, and established coordinated high pressure does not become the dominant identity without the context passing to RPC-002.
Several progression routes stay available (at least two).
Goalkeeper involvement is typical but not independently defining.
The coach's player count and playing area reach the game unchanged, and a count that cannot be split is refused with a sentence.

manipulations.source: RC1.1 Representative Performance Context Library (docx), RPC-001 Goalkeeper Build-Out, Typical Interaction Regulations, Common: 'defensive release timing' (no rule given)
manipulations.statusBasis: His 16 October reply, item 3: 'For the first activity, I favor allowing immediate pressing from a representative starting arrangement, with starting positions and distances used to regulate the challenge.' 'I do not favor a timed release.' 'However, please do not automatically add a high-regain bonus.'
manipulations.note: Immediate pressing needs no mechanism: nothing in the game restricts when the opposition may press (RPC-001 declares S4 access, V11 and V23-V26 NON_CLAIMED and V25 NOT_AUTHORED). A designated pressure line and release when the goalkeeper plays the ball are kept as potential realizations only, and not built (item 3). No existing knowledge authorizes a high-regain incentive, and none is added. Amended 17 October 2026 (stage M2): his reply filed 19 October 2026, item 2, now authorizes one, as a score of ordinary value and not a bonus: "This gives the pressing team a meaningful incentive to recognize and exploit high-regain opportunities without requiring an arbitrary additional pass or dribble." It is carried by A01-R1-V27-1 (a controlled regain inside the pressing team's own target counts as a score); no value is changed, so his item 3 above still holds. The starting arrangement that regulates the challenge is the defending team's starting relationship above (D4, M5). Nothing yet tells the coach that pressing may begin immediately: the renderer states no NON_CLAIMED declaration. Until 15 October 2026 (stage H3) this was MISSING_KNOWLEDGE; his item 3 answers it.

evaluation.words: I would like to evaluate the resulting activity as a coach, particularly:

points.words: Whether the goalkeeper is a functional supporting option.
Whether attacking players have meaningful opportunities to recognize and solve pressure.
Whether the opposing team creates realistic defensive problems.
Whether the progression and post-regain scoring conditions create the intended consequences.
Whether any artificial shortcuts emerge, including the advanced-positioning concern described above.

words.words: Please flag whether the generated activity permits players to remain beyond the progression line without any meaningful defensive interaction.
We can evaluate the actual activity and decide whether a spatial eligibility regulation is necessary.

If one is needed, we should first determine whether the existing Interaction Regulation knowledge supports it. Any implementation should express a reusable relationship, not a special Play Out from the Back exception.
I agree that the unresolved regain-inside-target case should remain flagged for review rather than be settled through an invented rule.
A successful regain alone should not count as controlled progression into the target area.
Nor should we require an additional pass simply because a regain occurred inside or near the target.
The scoring event should evaluate the actual controlled progression outcome.

settledBy.words: The pressing team retains its separate objective of regaining possession and attacking the 5 m target area.
For the previously flagged corner case, I favor allowing a controlled regain inside that area to count as a score, provided the pressing team genuinely establishes possession.
A contested touch, deflection, or loose ball should not qualify.
This is a provisional scoring choice for the current realization, not a universal rule equating every regain with successful progression.

words.words: The second-goalkeeper case and optional rotation can remain visible as limitations for now. I don't want to prescribe an outfield role for a goalkeeper universally.

I acknowledge that attackers can currently remain beyond the progression line. Let's evaluate whether this produces an unrepresentative shortcut before authorizing a spatial eligibility or offside mechanism.

I understand that the activity currently runs through the checked review pathway, not the live app. The mandatory library-constraint requirement remains a separate systemic issue to resolve before pilot delivery.

pathway.words: Similarly, I understand that the checked review pathway is not yet the live application pathway because of the outstanding constraint requirement. Please keep that distinction visible as we approach acceptance.

words: The objective is not to demonstrate that the engine can satisfy a collection of rules. It is to demonstrate that those rules produce a representative learning environment.
Once the activity is generated, we can evaluate its learning-design quality before extending the work to additional goals or variations.

rationale.feature: The building team has more players than the pressing team (the starting configuration)

words.words: In match play, teams building from the back commonly have more players available in their defensive third than the opposition initially commits to pressing.
That numerical relationship can create opportunities to circulate possession, attract pressure, recycle through the goalkeeper, and find a different route forward.
A building-team numerical advantage is therefore not necessarily an artificial simplification. It can be representative of the actual performance environment.

rationale.feature: One active specialized player, always with the building team

words.words: The goalkeeper should be available as a deep supporting passing option.
Players may use the goalkeeper to recycle possession, draw pressure, change the point of attack, or create a new progression opportunity.
Those are available solutions, not required behaviors.

rationale.feature: One team builds out while the other presses, exchanged by block

words.words: The reason for choosing asymmetry initially is to increase the frequency of meaningful encounters with the build-out problem while preserving active opposition and the consequences of losing possession.
